gloss: to characterize; to be distinctive of

definitions.gloss: to characterize, to distinguish, to make distinctive
definitions.explanation: To give something its distinctive character or quality, or to serve as a defining feature of something.

examples.japanese: この{作品|さくひん}を{特徴|とくちょう}づけるのは{独特|どくとく}な{色使|いろづか}いだ。
examples.english: What characterizes this work is its unique use of color.

examples.japanese: {多様性|たようせい}が{現代|げんだい}{社会|しゃかい}を{特徴|とくちょう}づけている。
{急速|きゅうそく}な{技術|ぎじゅつ}{革新|かくしん}と{情報|じょうほう}の{大量|たいりょう}{消費|しょうひ}が、この{時代|じだい}を{特徴|とくちょう}づけていると{言|い}えるだろう。
examples.english: One could say that rapid technological innovation and massive information consumption characterize this era.

notes:
Formed from the noun {特徴|とくちょう} (characteristic, feature) plus the verb-forming suffix づける (to give, to attach). This is an ichidan verb. Common in academic writing, essays, and analytical discussion.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {時代|じだい}を{特徴|とくちょう}づける: to characterize an era
- {文化|ぶんか}を{特徴|とくちょう}づける: to define a culture
- {作品|さくひん}を{特徴|とくちょう}づける: to characterize a work

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {特徴|とくちょう}がある: to have a characteristic — describes having features, rather than defining something by them
- {象徴|しょうちょう}する: to symbolize — represents something abstractly rather than defining its nature
- {定義|ていぎ}する: to define — more precise and logical; used for formal definitions
